questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about the units of temperature?
choices: Degree Celsius is written with a capital letter.
Kelvin is written with a capital letter.
Degree Fahrenheit is written with a lower-case letter.
The symbol for Kelvin is written as K.
questions.solution: The correct option is that the symbol for Kelvin is written as K. The Kelvin unit is represented by the capital letter K, while the word 'kelvin' itself is written with a lowercase letter. 'Degree Celsius' and 'degree Fahrenheit' are written with lowercase 'degree' and uppercase 'Celsius' or 'Fahrenheit', and 'Kelvin' as a word is lowercase, not uppercase.

questions.stem: A laboratory thermometer is placed in a beaker of water. What is the correct procedure for reading the temperature?
choices: Read the temperature after removing the thermometer from the water.
Ensure the bulb touches the bottom of the beaker.
Read the temperature while the thermometer is immersed in water.
questions.solution: The correct procedure is to read the temperature while the thermometer is immersed in water because the bulb needs to be in contact with the liquid to accurately measure its temperature. Reading after removing the thermometer is incorrect because the temperature can drop rapidly once it is no longer in the water. Holding the thermometer horizontally or having the bulb touch the bottom of the beaker can lead to inaccurate readings due to improper heat transfer or contact.

questions.stem: A student uses a laboratory thermometer to measure the temperature of a chemical reaction. The temperature rises from 20°C to 40°C in 10 minutes. What is the average rate of temperature increase per minute?
questions.solution: The average rate of temperature increase is calculated by dividing the total temperature change by the time taken. The temperature increases by 20°C over 10 minutes, so the rate is 20°C / 10 min = 2°C/min. The other options are incorrect because they do not match the calculation.

questions.stem: If a clinical thermometer is not properly cleaned before and after use, what is the most likely consequence?
choices: It may show a false high reading
It may show a false low reading
It may show a false reading due to contamination
questions.solution: If a clinical thermometer is not properly cleaned, it may give inaccurate readings because residual substances can interfere with the measurement. False high or low readings are possible but not the most likely direct consequence. Contamination may affect accuracy, but the primary issue is the inaccuracy of the reading itself.

questions.stem: A clinical thermometer shows a temperature of 37.0 °C for a healthy person. What would be the temperature in Fahrenheit scale?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 98.6 °F. This is because the standard formula to convert Celsius to Fahrenheit is °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32, and applying this to 37.0 °C gives 98.6 °F. The other options are incorrect because they do not result from using the correct conversion formula.

hi.solution: सही उत्तर 98.6 °F है। यह इसलिए है क्योंकि सेल्सियस को फारेनहाइट में बदलने का मानक सूत्र °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32 है, और 37.0 °C के लिए इसका उपयोग करने पर 98.6 °F प्राप्त होता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि वे सही रूप से संकेत सूत्र के उपयोग से नहीं प्राप्त होते हैं।

mr.solution: योग्य उत्तर 98.6 °F आहे. कारण सेल्सियस तापमान फॅरेनहाइटमध्ये रूपांतरित करण्याचा मानक सूत्र °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32 आहे, आणि 37.0 °C ला याचा अवलंब केल्यास 98.6 °F मिळतो. इतर उत्तरे चुकीची आहेत कारण ते योग्य रूपांतरित करण्याच्या सूत्राचा अवलंब केल्याने मिळत नाहीत.
